elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d) requires Contractor to defend Company and its affiliates against any third-party claim alleging that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against losses resulting from third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d) requires Contractor to indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates from such claims and all resulting damages, costs, and expenses, including reasonable attorneys' fees.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The defense obligation applies to any third-party claim arising from Contractor's breach of applicable law.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against losses resulting from third-party claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: The indemnification obligation expressly covers Contractor's breach of applicable law and resulting damages, costs, and expenses.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(iii) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Company data or Confidential Information caused by Contractor, and the lead-in applies the defense obligation to those third-party claims.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against losses resulting from a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(iii) covers Contractor-caused unauthorized access or disclosure and indemnifies Company and its affiliates for resulting damages, costs, and expenses.

elements.element: Vendor must defend Customer and its affiliates against third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(iv) expressly covers Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct under the defense obligation.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer and its affiliates against losses resulting from third-party claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(iv) expressly covers Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct under the indemnification obligation.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide notice of the claim.
elements.evidence: Company must provide Contractor with prompt written notice of the claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of the defense and settlement.
elements.evidence: Contractor receives sole control of the defense and settlement, subject to Company consent for settlements imposing an obligation or admission on Company.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer to provide reasonable cooperation.
elements.evidence: Company must provide reasonable cooperation at Contractor's expense.

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity must be limited to Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law, with no broader indemnity grounds.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause imposes no indemnity obligation on Company. The condition is therefore demonstrably absent, and Company is not exposed to any broader indemnity grounds.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d)(i) provides an IP indemnity for claims alleging that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by Customer's modification of the services or deliverables.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims caused by combining the services or deliverables with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combination exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must exclude claims arising from Vendor's compliance with Customer-provided specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: For an infringing service or deliverable, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to procure Customer's continued right to use it.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no obligation or option to procure continued usage rights.

elements.element: For an infringing service or deliverable, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to modify it so that it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: For an infringing service or deliverable, Vendor must have or provide a remedy to replace it with a non-infringing substitute.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: For an infringing service or deliverable, Vendor must have or provide a refund remedy.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Section 7(d) instead states that Contractor's indemnification obligations are not subject to Section 7(a)'s liability limitation, and it supplies no 3× annual-fees cap.

result.reason: The operative language fully reaches the preferred position: it provides defense and indemnification for all required third-party claim categories, covers Company and its affiliates, and includes notice, control, and cooperation procedures. No Customer indemnity exists, so Customer is not exposed beyond the permitted grounds. The fallback is not satisfied because all stated IP exclusions, the procure/modify/replace/refund remedy package, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap are absent. The redline is not minimal because it also makes the indemnity uncapped, a substantive liability-cap change not expressly required by the preferred elements. Intent is otherwise preserved through express, coordinated carve-outs from the existing cap and attorneys' fee waiver. Drafting quality is reduced by the misleading title 'Indemnification of Contractor,' repeated subsection lettering, and the awkward placement of the warranty subsection before the Section 7 heading.
